title: rorca-postgres-migration
description: Replace SQLite with PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector + Apache AGE as Rorca's unified data layer. Three pillars: (1) Relational — async pg Pool replaces sync better-sqlite3 across all 45 routes and 15 lib modules. (2) Semantic — pgvector embeddings + tsvector full-text + Reciprocal Rank Fusion hybrid search replace sqlite-vec and FTS5. (3) Graph — Apache AGE knowledge graph captures story→file→memory→convention relationships for context-aware retrieval and drift detection. Plus a tiered memory architecture: CAG (hot in-memory cache for direction + recent context) + RAG (cold vector search for historical memory) with automatic fallback routing. Docker Compose for zero-config install, SQLite data migration tool, Supabase/Neon cloud compatibility. Supersedes PR-003, PR-011–017, PR-049–050 from rorca-production-ready.

userStories.title: PostgreSQL Schema — Convert All Migrations
userStories.description: As the system, I need all 36 SQLite migrations converted to PostgreSQL dialect — so the entire schema can be created on a fresh Postgres 16 database.
acceptanceCriteria: New directory backend/src/db/pg-migrations/ created with 36 numbered SQL files matching existing 001–036 migration sequence

All SQLite-specific syntax converted: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT → SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, datetime('now') → NOW(), BOOLEAN with 0/1 → BOOLEAN with true/false, TEXT fields storing JSON → JSONB where appropriate (wal_events.payload, spec_versions.snapshot, onboarding_state.data, user_settings.preferences, etc.)
SQLite PRAGMA statements removed (journal_mode=WAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout) — Postgres handles these natively (WAL is default, FK always enforced, connection pooling handles contention)

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING fts5(...) replaced with: tsvector column on the same table + GIN index + trigger function to auto-update tsvector on INSERT/UPDATE. Apply to every table that had FTS5: specs (title + description), wal_events (payload text extraction), story_results (story title + output), archive entries
All IF NOT EXISTS clauses preserved (Postgres supports them natively on CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX, CREATE EXTENSION)
json_extract() calls in migration CHECK constraints or defaults converted to JSONB operators: ->> for text extraction, -> for JSON object extraction, @> for containment, ? for key existence

A migration runner in backend/src/db/pg-index.ts: connects via pg Pool, creates schema_migrations table (version INT, applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ, filename TEXT), runs each .sql file in numeric order, wraps each in a transaction (rollback on failure), skips already-applied versions, logs progress to stdout
Migration 037 added: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto; (for gen_random_uuid if needed by any existing logic)
All 37 migrations apply cleanly on a fresh Postgres 16 database with zero errors
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Database Connection Layer — pg Pool + Async Helpers
userStories.description: As a backend developer, I need a Postgres connection pool with async query helpers that mirror the current better-sqlite3 API shape — so the route conversion (PG-003/004) is mechanical rather than architectural.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/db/index.ts rewritten: exports a pg Pool instance configured from DATABASE_URL env var (default: postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5432/rorca), pool size 20 (matches Postgres default max_connections=100, leaving room for other clients), idle timeout 30s, connection timeout 5s, statement_timeout 30s (prevents runaway queries)

Helper functions exported that mirror current usage patterns: query<T>(sql: string, params?: any[]) → Promise<T[]> (replaces db.prepare(sql).all(...)), queryOne<T>(sql: string, params?: any[]) → Promise<T | undefined> (replaces db.prepare(sql).get(...)), execute(sql: string, params?: any[]) → Promise<{ rowCount: number }> (replaces db.prepare(sql).run(...)), transaction<T>(fn: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>) → Promise<T> (replaces db.transaction(() => {...})() — acquires client, BEGIN, runs fn, COMMIT or ROLLBACK, releases client)

All helpers use parameterized queries with $1, $2, ... numbered placeholders (NOT string interpolation). A utility function rewritePlaceholders(sql) that converts ? to $1, $2, ... is available for incremental migration but should NOT be used in final code — all queries should use $N natively
Connection lifecycle: pool created lazily on first query (not on import — prevents startup crash if DB is slow), pool.end() called on SIGTERM/SIGINT for clean shutdown

Pool health check: export async function dbHealthCheck(): Promise<{ ok: boolean, latencyMs: number, poolStats: { total, idle, waiting } }> — runs SELECT 1 and returns diagnostics. Used by GET /api/health

Environment variable precedence: DATABASE_URL (full connection string) > individual vars (PGHOST, PGPORT, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, PGDATABASE) > defaults (localhost:5432/rorca, user: rorca, password: rorca). SSL: enabled automatically when DATABASE_URL contains sslmode=require or when PGSSLMODE=require (needed for Supabase/Neon)
On pool creation, runs migration runner from PG-001 automatically — same auto-migration pattern as current SQLite, but async (awaits completion before first query resolves)
The old better-sqlite3 db object export is removed. Any file importing from db/index.ts gets the new async Pool and helpers
Logging: slow query warning (> 500ms) logged with query text and params (sanitized — no password/secret values). Configurable via SLOW_QUERY_THRESHOLD_MS env var
backend/src/db/index.ts compiles with no TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Route Async Conversion — Wave 1 (Core Routes)
userStories.description: As a user, I need the most-used API routes to work with PostgreSQL — so core workflows (specs, pipeline, workspaces, direction, WAL) function immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: The following route files converted from sync better-sqlite3 to async pg Pool: specs.ts, pipeline.ts, workspaces.ts, direction.ts, wal.ts, health.ts, context.ts, onboarding.ts
Every db.prepare(sql).get(...) → await queryOne<Type>(sql, [params]) with $1,$2 numbered placeholders
Every db.prepare(sql).all(...) → await query<Type>(sql, [params]) with $1,$2 numbered placeholders
Every db.prepare(sql).run(...) → await execute(sql, [params]) with $1,$2 numbered placeholders
Every db.transaction(() => { ... })() → await transaction(async (client) => { ... }) with all inner queries using client.query() on the transactional client, not the shared pool
All route handler signatures updated: (req, res) => { ... } → async (req, res, next) => { try { ... } catch(err) { next(err) } } — or use express-async-errors for automatic forwarding

SQLite-specific SQL functions converted: json_extract(col, '$.key') → col->>'key' (JSONB text), json_extract(col, '$.key') returning JSON → col->'key', GROUP_CONCAT(col, sep) → STRING_AGG(col, sep), datetime('now') → NOW(), datetime('now', '-N days') → NOW() - INTERVAL 'N days', IFNULL → COALESCE, LIKE → ILIKE where case-insensitive matching is intended
Archive search: FTS5 MATCH query replaced with tsvector @@ plainto_tsquery() using the GIN index from PG-001. ts_headline() used for snippet generation with highlighted matches
WAL events: ts column (TIMESTAMPTZ in Postgres) — ORDER BY ts DESC preserved, date range filters use BETWEEN with TIMESTAMPTZ comparison

Pagination queries: LIMIT/OFFSET syntax identical between SQLite and Postgres — no change needed, but verify COUNT(*) OVER() window functions work for total count (Postgres supports them natively, more efficient than separate COUNT query)
All 8 route files compile with no TypeScript errors
Smoke test: POST /api/specs/generate, GET /api/specs/archive, POST /api/pipeline/trigger, GET /api/workspaces, GET/PUT /api/direction return correct data against Postgres

userStories.title: pgvector Extension + Embedding Store
userStories.description: As the system, I need a vector storage layer in Postgres — so specs, stories, and memory entries can be semantically searched by meaning, not just keywords.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration 038 added: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;

Migration 038 creates embeddings table: id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, source_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source_type IN ('spec', 'story', 'memory', 'archive', 'convention', 'file')), source_id TEXT NOT NULL, workspace_id INTEGER REFERENCES workspaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, content_hash TEXT NOT NULL (SHA-256 of embedded text — dedup/staleness), embedding vector(1536) NOT NULL, model TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'text-embedding-3-small', metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}' (flexible: store relevance scores, category, tags), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
Composite UNIQUE constraint on (source_type, source_id, workspace_id) — one embedding per source per workspace, upsert on content change
HNSW index: CREATE INDEX idx_embeddings_hnsw ON embeddings USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64) — fast approximate nearest neighbor with cosine similarity
Partial indexes for filtered searches: CREATE INDEX idx_embeddings_type ON embeddings (source_type, workspace_id) — speeds up type-filtered vector queries

Helper module backend/src/db/embeddings.ts exports: upsertEmbedding(sourceType, sourceId, workspaceId, text, embedding, model, metadata?), findSimilar(queryEmbedding, options: { sourceTypes?, workspaceId?, limit?, threshold? }) → Array<{ sourceType, sourceId, similarity, metadata }>, deleteEmbedding(sourceType, sourceId, workspaceId), deleteByWorkspace(workspaceId), isStale(sourceType, sourceId, workspaceId, currentTextHash) → boolean

findSimilar query: SELECT source_type, source_id, metadata, 1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) AS similarity FROM embeddings WHERE workspace_id = $2 AND ($3::text[] IS NULL OR source_type = ANY($3)) AND 1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) > $4 ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector LIMIT $5
Dimension configurable via EMBEDDING_DIMENSION env var: 1536 (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small), 3072 (OpenAI text-embedding-3-large), 1024 (Voyage AI voyage-3). Default 1536
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Embedding Pipeline — Generate + Store Vectors
userStories.description: As the system, I need an embedding generation pipeline that creates vectors for specs, stories, and memory entries — so semantic search and the knowledge graph have data to work with.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/embedding-pipeline.ts created with: embedText(text: string) → Promise<number[]>, embedBatch(texts: string[]) → Promise<number[][]> (batch up to 100 texts per API call for efficiency)

Provider support via EMBEDDING_PROVIDER env var: 'openai' (default) uses text-embedding-3-small ($0.02/1M tokens), 'openai-large' uses text-embedding-3-large, 'voyage' uses voyage-3 (requires VOYAGE_API_KEY). Provider interface allows adding new providers without changing pipeline logic

API key resolution chain: (1) vault_keys table (AES-256-GCM encrypted, per-workspace) → (2) env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY, VOYAGE_API_KEY) → (3) error with helpful message ('No embedding API key configured. Add one in Settings > Providers or set OPENAI_API_KEY')

Automatic embedding triggers via SSE hub subscription: spec_approved → embed each story (title + description + acceptance criteria concatenated), run_finished → re-embed stories with pass/fail outcome context appended, memory entry created/updated → embed entry text, archive entry created → embed spec summary + final status

Job queue with backpressure: embedding jobs queued in-memory (Array<EmbedJob>), processed sequentially with configurable rate limit (EMBEDDING_RATE_LIMIT, default 50/min). Queue depth exposed via GET /api/health (embeddings: { queueDepth, processed, failed })
Staleness check: before embedding, compute SHA-256 of input text, call isStale() — if hash matches existing row, skip (saves API cost). Re-embed only when content actually changed

Error handling: embedding API failures (rate limit, network, auth) are logged as warnings, retry 3x with exponential backoff (1s, 4s, 16s), then skip. Parent operation (spec approval, run completion) is NEVER blocked or failed by embedding errors — embeddings are best-effort enhancement

Backfill endpoint: POST /api/admin/embed-all queues embedding jobs for all existing specs, stories, memory entries, and archived specs in the workspace. Returns { queued: number, skippedStale: number }. Progress trackable via GET /api/admin/embed-all/status
Text preparation: embedText strips markdown formatting, truncates to 8000 tokens (embedding model limit), prepends source type as prefix ('story: ...', 'memory: ...') for better embedding quality
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Hybrid Search — tsvector + pgvector + RRF
userStories.description: As a user searching for specs or stories, I want results that understand meaning — so 'payment retry' finds 'transaction failure handling' even though the words don't match.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/search.ts created with: hybridSearch(query: string, options: { sourceTypes?: string[], workspaceId?: number, limit?: number, keywordWeight?: number, semanticWeight?: number }) → Promise<SearchResult[]> where SearchResult = { sourceType, sourceId, title, snippet, score, matchType: 'keyword' | 'semantic' | 'hybrid', highlights?: string[] }

Keyword leg: Postgres tsvector with plainto_tsquery('english', query). Ranks via ts_rank_cd(tsvector, query, 32) (cover density ranking). Returns top 30 candidates. Uses ts_headline() for snippet generation with <mark> tags for highlighting
Semantic leg: embeds query text via embedText(), calls findSimilar() with cosine threshold 0.25. Returns top 30 candidates with similarity scores

Reciprocal Rank Fusion merging: RRF_score = Σ(weight / (k + rank)). k=60 (standard constant). keywordWeight default 1.0, semanticWeight default 1.0 (equal weighting, adjustable per query). Results appearing in BOTH lists get boosted (dual presence is a strong relevance signal). Final output sorted by RRF_score descending, truncated to limit (default 20)

GET /api/search endpoint: query params — q (required), type (optional filter: spec|story|memory|archive|convention), workspace (optional workspace ID), limit (default 20), mode (keyword|semantic|hybrid, default hybrid). Response: { results: SearchResult[], meta: { keywordHits, semanticHits, hybridHits, latencyMs } }

Archive search (GET /api/specs/archive) updated: existing search param now feeds hybridSearch with sourceType=['archive']. Preserves all existing query params (status, tags, page, pageSize) — search is additive on top of filters
Story search (used in Forge story browser, Command Palette): hybridSearch with sourceType=['story']
Memory search (used in Direction > Memory tab): hybridSearch with sourceType=['memory']

Graceful degradation: if embeddings table is empty or embedding pipeline not configured, hybridSearch auto-falls back to keyword-only (tsvector). Logs warning once: 'No embeddings found — search using keywords only. Run POST /api/admin/embed-all to enable semantic search'
Performance: hybrid search returns in < 200ms for 500 specs + 5000 stories + 2000 memory entries (verified via test with pg_stat_statements timing)
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Docker Compose — Postgres 16 + pgvector + AGE
userStories.description: As a user installing Rorca, I want one command (docker compose up) to get a fully working instance — Postgres with all extensions, the Rorca server, and zero manual setup.
acceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.yml at repo root with two services: 'db' and 'rorca'

db service: custom Dockerfile (docker/postgres/Dockerfile) based on pgvector/pgvector:pg16, adds Apache AGE extension build (apt-get install postgresql-16-age or compile from source if package unavailable), port 5432:5432, named volume rorca_pgdata for persistence, environment: POSTGRES_USER=rorca, POSTGRES_PASSWORD=rorca, POSTGRES_DB=rorca, healthcheck: pg_isready -U rorca -d rorca (interval 5s, timeout 3s, retries 5)

rorca service: builds from Dockerfile at repo root, depends_on db with condition: service_healthy, port 3030:3030, environment: DATABASE_URL=postgres://rorca:rorca@db:5432/rorca, RORCA_SERVE_STATIC=1, NODE_ENV=production

Rorca Dockerfile: multi-stage — Stage 1 (build): node:20-alpine, WORKDIR /app, COPY package*.json, npm ci, COPY ., npm run build (frontend Vite build), cd backend && npm ci && npx tsc. Stage 2 (runtime): node:20-alpine, COPY --from=build /app/dist /app/dist, COPY --from=build /app/backend /app/backend, COPY cli.js package.json, EXPOSE 3030, CMD node cli.js start --no-open. userStories.title: Selective Retrieval in synthesize()
userStories.description: As the execution engine, I need synthesize() to use semantic search to pick the most relevant context — instead of dumping everything into the prompt and blowing up token budgets.
acceptanceCriteria: synthesize() in direction-stack.ts gains an optional parameter: synthesize(workspaceId, options?: { storyText?: string, maxTokens?: number }) → Promise<SynthesizedContext>. Return type changes from raw string to { text: string, metadata: ContextMetadata }

ContextMetadata type: { totalTokens: number, layers: { standards: boolean, conventions: boolean, project: boolean }, memoryEntries: { included: number, total: number, relevanceRange: [number, number] }, droppedItems: Array<{ type: string, reason: string }>, searchMode: 'semantic' | 'keyword' | 'full-dump' }

When storyText is provided: calls hybridSearch(storyText, { sourceTypes: ['memory'], workspaceId, limit: 15 }) to retrieve the 15 most relevant memory entries instead of ALL entries. Only entries with similarity > 0.3 are included (below that threshold, they're noise)
When storyText is NOT provided (e.g., spec generation with no story context): includes the 20 most recent memory entries by timestamp (recency heuristic) instead of all entries

Token budget enforcement: maxTokens default 32000. Priority order for inclusion: (1) Direction layers — Standards/Conventions/Project, NEVER dropped, they're the foundation. (2) Memory entries — sorted by relevance score descending, included until budget exhausted. (3) Scoped files from context router — sorted by scope priority descending, included until budget exhausted. Dropped items recorded in metadata with reason ('token_budget_exceeded', 'below_relevance_threshold')
Token estimation: text.length / 4 (same ~4 chars/token heuristic used in context-router.ts — consistent across codebase)

For workspaces with no embeddings (fresh install, no API key): searchMode falls back to 'full-dump' but WITH the token budget cap — truncates at maxTokens instead of unlimited. Logs warning: 'No embeddings configured — using full memory dump with token budget cap'
synthesize() output for a workspace with 200+ memory entries stays under maxTokens (previously unbounded). Verified with test case
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors. All callers of synthesize() updated to handle the new return type

userStories.title: CAG — In-Memory Context Cache (Hot Layer)
userStories.description: As the execution engine, I need frequently-accessed context cached in memory — so direction layers, active workspace config, and recent memory entries are available instantly without a database query on every story prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/context-cache.ts created implementing a tiered cache with explicit hot/warm/cold classification. Cache is a singleton Map<string, CacheEntry> with TTL-based expiration

Hot tier (always cached, TTL 5 min, auto-refresh): direction layers per workspace (Standards, Conventions, Project — the data that changes least but is read on EVERY story prompt), workspace config (.rorca/config.json parsed routing rules), active agent profile for current run

Warm tier (cached on first access, TTL 2 min): memory entries from last 30 days (the 'working memory' — most likely to be relevant), installed skills list per workspace, workspace echolocation report (stack detection)
Cold tier (not cached — always goes to DB/vector search): historical memory entries older than 30 days, archived specs, WAL events, analytics data. These are accessed via RAG (PG-012/PG-014)

Cache API: get<T>(key: string) → T | null, set(key: string, value, tier: 'hot' | 'warm', ttlMs?: number), invalidate(key: string), invalidatePattern(glob: string) (e.g., invalidatePattern('workspace:5:*') clears all cache for workspace 5), warmup(workspaceId: number) → Promise<void> (pre-loads all hot + warm entries for a workspace)

Automatic invalidation: when direction layers are updated (PUT /api/direction), cache key workspace:{id}:direction:* invalidated. When memory is updated, workspace:{id}:memory:recent invalidated. When config.json changes, workspace:{id}:config invalidated. Invalidation is triggered by the route handlers after successful DB write — no stale reads
Cache statistics: cacheStats() → { hits, misses, hitRate, entries, memoryBytes } — exposed in GET /api/health response under cache: { ... }

synthesize() updated (from PG-012): checks cache FIRST for direction layers and recent memory before falling through to DB query. Cache hit = ~0ms, DB query = ~5-15ms. Expected hit rate > 90% during pipeline runs (same workspace context reused across stories)
Memory footprint: cache is bounded. Max 1000 entries, LRU eviction when exceeded. Estimated memory: ~2-5MB for a workspace with rich context (acceptable for a single-user self-hosted tool)
Pipeline run warmup: when a pipeline run starts (POST /api/pipeline/trigger), call warmup(workspaceId) to pre-populate cache — all stories in the run benefit from cache hits from story 1
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Memory Tiering Router — CAG/RAG Fallback Chain
userStories.description: As the execution engine, I need a unified memory retrieval function that checks the fast cache first, then falls back to vector search — so every story gets the best available context with minimum latency.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/memory-router.ts created with: retrieveContext(workspaceId: number, storyText: string, options?: { maxTokens?: number, includeGraph?: boolean }) → Promise<RetrievedContext>

RetrievedContext type: { direction: { standards, conventions, project }, memory: MemoryEntry[], skills: SkillContent[], graphContext?: GraphContext, meta: { cagHits: number, ragHits: number, graphHits: number, totalTokens: number, latencyMs: number, tier: 'cache' | 'search' | 'hybrid' } }

Retrieval chain (executed in order, stops when token budget is met): Step 1 — CAG: read direction layers + recent memory + skills from context-cache.ts (PG-013). If cache hit for all, return immediately (tier: 'cache', latency ~1ms). Step 2 — if story references unfamiliar concepts (not found in cached memory): RAG search via hybridSearch (PG-008) for relevant cold memory entries. Merge with cached hot entries, deduplicate by source_id. Step 3 — if includeGraph is true: query knowledge graph (PG-015) for related stories, file touches, convention links. Append as structured context

'Unfamiliar concept' detection: extract key noun phrases from storyText (simple heuristic: split by spaces, filter stopwords, take nouns > 4 chars), check if any appear in cached memory entries. If < 50% of key phrases have cache coverage, trigger RAG search. This prevents unnecessary vector searches when cached context is sufficient

Token budget: direction layers always included (non-negotiable). Remaining budget split: 60% memory (CAG + RAG), 25% skills, 15% graph context. If any category underflows, budget redistributed to others

synthesize() in direction-stack.ts refactored: now calls retrieveContext() internally instead of manually assembling layers + memory + search. synthesize() becomes a thin wrapper: calls retrieveContext() → formats into prompt string → returns SynthesizedContext (preserving existing return type contract)
Latency targets: cache-only path < 5ms, cache + RAG < 100ms, cache + RAG + graph < 200ms. Logged in meta for observability

userStories.title: Apache AGE Extension + Knowledge Graph Schema
userStories.description: As the system, I need a graph layer in Postgres that captures relationships between stories, files, memory entries, and conventions — so context retrieval can traverse connections instead of only matching keywords or vectors.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration 039: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS age; SET search_path = ag_catalog, public; SELECT create_graph('rorca');

Graph node types (vertices) created via Cypher: (:Story {id, specId, title, status}), (:File {path, workspace_id}), (:Memory {id, category, created_at}), (:Spec {id, title, status, workspace_id}), (:Convention {name, source, layer}), (:Workspace {id, label}), (:Skill {name, source})

Graph edge types (relationships): (Story)-[:TOUCHES]->(File) — populated from story_commits + git diff analysis, (Story)-[:BELONGS_TO]->(Spec), (Story)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(Story) — mirrors dependsOn from spec JSON, (Memory)-[:LEARNED_FROM]->(Story) — memory entries linked to the story run that produced them, (Memory)-[:ABOUT]->(File) — memory entries referencing specific files, (Convention)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(File) — conventions linked to file patterns they govern, (Convention)-[:VIOLATED_BY]->(Story) — detected convention violations, (Skill)-[:USED_IN]->(Story) — tracks which skills were injected per story, (Spec)-[:IN_WORKSPACE]->(Workspace)

backend/src/lib/knowledge-graph.ts exports: addStoryNode(story), addFileTouch(storyId, filePath), addMemoryLink(memoryId, storyId), addConventionLink(conventionName, filePath), queryRelated(nodeType, nodeId, depth?, edgeTypes?) → CypherResult[], queryImpact(filePath) → Array<{stories, specs, conventions}> (fan-out query: what stories/specs/conventions are connected to this file?)

Cypher queries executed via: SELECT * FROM cypher('rorca', $$ MATCH (s:Story {id: $1})-[:TOUCHES]->(f:File) RETURN f.path $$) AS (path agtype) — Apache AGE's SQL/Cypher bridge. All queries parameterized (no Cypher injection)

Graph population triggers: on run_finished WAL event → parse story_commits for file paths → create (:Story)-[:TOUCHES]->(:File) edges. On memory synthesis → create (:Memory)-[:LEARNED_FROM]->(:Story) edges. On spec approval → create (:Story)-[:BELONGS_ON]->(:Spec) and (:Story)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(:Story) edges from dependsOn field
Graph is additive — never deleted, only appended. Historical edges preserved for temporal analysis ('which stories touched auth.ts over the last 5 specs?')
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors. agtype results properly typed via helper function parseAgtype<T>(result: agtype) → T

userStories.title: Graph-Powered Context Retrieval
userStories.description: As the execution engine, I need graph traversal to enrich story context — so when a story touches auth.ts, it automatically gets memory entries from previous stories that also touched auth.ts, plus relevant conventions.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/graph-context.ts created with: getGraphContext(storyId: string, predictedPaths: string[], workspaceId: number, maxDepth?: number) → Promise<GraphContext>

GraphContext type: { relatedMemories: Array<{ memoryId, text, relationship, hops }>, relatedConventions: Array<{ name, content, appliesTo }>, fileHistory: Array<{ path, touchedByStories: string[], lastModifiedSpec }>, impactRadius: number (number of unique connected nodes) }

Path-based traversal: for each predicted file path from the story, query: MATCH (f:File {path: $1})<-[:TOUCHES]-(s:Story)-[:LEARNED_FROM]->(m:Memory) RETURN m — finds memory entries from stories that previously touched the same files. Depth-limited to maxDepth (default 2 hops — direct connections + one intermediate node)

Convention lookup: for each predicted path, query: MATCH (f:File {path: $1})<-[:APPLIES_TO]-(c:Convention) RETURN c — finds conventions governing files this story will touch. Returned conventions injected as 'Convention context: follow these patterns for files matching {glob}'

Conflict detection: query: MATCH (s1:Story {id: $1})-[:TOUCHES]->(f:File)<-[:TOUCHES]-(s2:Story) WHERE s1 <> s2 AND s2.status = 'running' RETURN f, s2 — detects if another in-progress story is touching the same files (useful for wave parallel execution conflict warnings)

Integration with memory-router.ts (PG-014): when includeGraph is true, retrieveContext() calls getGraphContext() and appends results to the context payload. Graph context is formatted as a distinct section: '## Related History (from knowledge graph)\n- auth.ts was modified by US-007 (auth middleware), which learned: [memory entry text]'
Performance: graph queries cached in context-cache.ts (warm tier, TTL 2 min) keyed by story ID + predicted paths hash. Re-queries only on cache miss. Target: < 50ms for graph traversal with 10K nodes

userStories.title: Graph-Based Convention Drift + Impact Analysis
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see when stories violate established conventions and understand the blast radius of changes — so I can catch drift before it accumulates.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/drift-detector.ts created with: detectDrift(specId: string, workspaceId: number) → Promise<DriftReport>. Runs AFTER a pipeline run completes (triggered by run_finished WAL event)

DriftReport type: { violations: Array<{ convention, file, story, severity: 'info' | 'warning' | 'error', description }>, impactAnalysis: Array<{ file, connectedStories: number, connectedSpecs: number, conventions: string[] }>, score: number (0-100, higher = more drift) }

Drift detection query: for each convention node, find stories from the just-completed spec that touched files governed by that convention: MATCH (c:Convention)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(f:File)<-[:TOUCHES]-(s:Story)-[:BELONGS_TO]->(spec:Spec {id: $1}) RETURN c, f, s — then check if the story's diff respects the convention (heuristic: convention keywords present in story output, or LLM-based validation if DRIFT_CHECK_LLM=true)

Impact analysis: for each file touched by the spec's stories, fan out: MATCH (f:File {path: $1})<-[:TOUCHES]-(s:Story)-[:BELONGS_TO]->(spec:Spec) RETURN COUNT(DISTINCT s), COUNT(DISTINCT spec) — shows how many other stories and specs have historically depended on this file (blast radius)

Convention violation edges: when drift is detected, create (:Convention)-[:VIOLATED_BY {spec_id, severity, timestamp}]->(:Story) edge in the graph — builds a historical record of drift for trend analysis
GET /api/workspaces/:id/drift endpoint: returns the most recent DriftReport for the workspace. Optional specId query param to get drift for a specific spec run

Frontend integration point: after a run completes, the Run View can show a 'Convention Health' tab with drift score and violation list (frontend story not included here — this is backend infrastructure)
POST /api/workspaces/:id/drift/check endpoint: manually trigger drift detection for the most recent completed spec (useful during development, not just post-run automation)

userStories.title: SQLite → Postgres Data Migration Tool
userStories.description: As an existing Rorca user upgrading from SQLite, I need a one-command migration tool that transfers all my data to the new Postgres database — so I don't lose workspaces, direction layers, run history, memory entries, or vault keys.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/scripts/migrate-sqlite-to-pg.ts created as a standalone script: npx tsx backend/src/scripts/migrate-sqlite-to-pg.ts --sqlite ./rorca.db --pg postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5432/rorca

Migration order respects foreign keys: (1) workspaces, (2) users + teams, (3) direction_layers, (4) specs-related tables (pipeline_runs, story_results, spec_versions, spec_tags, etc.), (5) wal_events, (6) vault_keys (transferred as-is — encrypted blobs), (7) settings + billing + notifications, (8) skills + agent_hooks + agent_profiles

Data transformation during migration: TEXT JSON columns → JSONB (parse and re-insert as JSONB), 0/1 booleans → true/false, datetime strings → TIMESTAMPTZ (parse ISO-8601, handle both SQLite datetime formats), INTEGER PRIMARY KEY → preserve original IDs (use OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE with explicit ID in INSERT to maintain referential integrity)
Batch processing: inserts in batches of 100 rows per transaction (prevents memory issues for large WAL tables — some users may have 100K+ WAL events)
Conflict handling: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for idempotent re-runs. Script can be run multiple times safely — skips existing rows, inserts new ones
Progress output: per-table progress bar (table_name: migrated N/total rows, elapsed Xs). Final summary: total rows migrated, tables processed, errors encountered

Error handling: per-row errors logged to migration-errors.log but don't stop migration. Summary shows count of skipped rows. Common errors: malformed JSON in payload columns (log and insert as TEXT fallback), missing foreign key targets (log and skip row)
Verification step: after migration, runs a check query per table comparing row counts between SQLite and Postgres. Reports discrepancies

Vault key migration: vault_keys rows copied as-is (encrypted blobs). The AES-256-GCM encryption is application-layer — same key/IV/tag works regardless of DB engine. Users don't need to re-enter API keys
Script exits with code 0 on success, code 1 on any errors (even if partial migration succeeded). Migration summary printed to stdout

userStories.title: Cloud Database Compatibility Layer
userStories.description: As a future cloud deployment, I need the Postgres integration to work with managed services (Supabase, Neon, Railway) — so the self-hosted → cloud path is a connection string swap with zero code changes.
acceptanceCriteria: SSL/TLS: when DATABASE_URL contains ?sslmode=require or PGSSLMODE=require is set, pg Pool uses ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false } for managed Postgres services that use self-signed CA certs (Supabase, Neon both require SSL but use custom CAs). When PGSSLROOTCERT is set, loads the CA cert file for strict verification

Connection pooling compatibility: managed services often have low connection limits (Supabase free: 50, Neon free: 100). Pool size auto-adjusts: reads max_connections from pg (SHOW max_connections), sets pool.max to min(configured_pool_size, max_connections * 0.8). Logs warning if configured size exceeds available connections

pgvector compatibility: Supabase includes pgvector natively (no CREATE EXTENSION needed on their managed instance). Neon supports pgvector as an extension. Migration runner: try CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector, catch and log (some managed services pre-install it and CREATE EXTENSION fails with 'already loaded')

Apache AGE compatibility: AGE is not available on most managed Postgres services (Supabase and Neon don't support it as of 2026). Compatibility layer: if CREATE EXTENSION age fails, set a flag GRAPH_AVAILABLE=false. All graph functions in knowledge-graph.ts check this flag and return empty results gracefully. Log warning: 'Apache AGE not available — graph features disabled. Use self-hosted Postgres for full graph support'. Core functionality (search, memory, CAG/RAG) works without the graph layer

Connection string parsing: support both formats — postgres://user:pass@host:port/db (standard) and postgresql://user:pass@host:port/db?sslmode=require (Supabase format). Parse query params for SSL, connection timeout, statement timeout

Health endpoint: reports managed service compatibility — { cloud: true/false, provider: 'supabase' | 'neon' | 'railway' | 'self-hosted' (inferred from hostname patterns), extensions: { vector: true, age: true/false }, connectionLimit: N }
Docker Compose is self-hosted only. For cloud, user sets DATABASE_URL in environment (or .env file) pointing to managed instance. No other config changes needed
Tested: migration runner runs cleanly against a fresh Supabase project (create project → set DATABASE_URL → npm run dev → verify health endpoint). Document the 3-step cloud setup in README

userStories.title: Memory Semantic Deduplication
userStories.description: As a user, I want MEMORY.md to not accumulate duplicate entries over time, so the memory stays clean and token-efficient. Implemented on pgvector — uses embedding similarity to detect duplicate memory entries.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/memory-dedup.ts created with: deduplicateMemory(entries) that identifies semantically duplicate entries and merges them
Deduplication strategy: compute embedding similarity between all pairs of memory entries. Entries with > 0.92 cosine similarity are considered duplicates
When duplicates found: keep the most recent entry, merge any unique details from older entries into the kept entry's text, add 'Merged from N entries' note
If vector search unavailable, fallback to exact text comparison (Levenshtein distance < 0.15 of string length)
POST /api/memory/deduplicate endpoint triggers deduplication on workspace memory, returns { removed: number, merged: number, total: number }
Deduplication runs automatically after memory synthesis (post-run), before writing to MEMORY.md
Dry-run mode: POST /api/memory/deduplicate?dryRun=true returns what would be removed without modifying anything
Memory panel shows 'Deduplicate' button that calls the endpoint and shows results
Backend TypeScript compiles with no errors

userStories.title: Cross-Workspace Memory Synthesis
userStories.description: As a user with multiple workspaces, I want insights from one workspace to inform others so architectural patterns learned in project A help project B. Implemented on pgvector + Apache AGE — uses graph traversal to synthesize memory across workspaces.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/cross-workspace-memory.ts created with: synthesizeCrossWorkspace(workspaceId) that finds relevant memory entries from other workspaces in the same domain (L2)
Cross-workspace entries are SUGGESTIONS only — they appear in Memory panel as 'From: {workspace label}' with Accept/Dismiss buttons
Matching criteria: same domain (e.g., both 'saas' L2) AND cosine similarity > 0.85 between memory entry and target workspace context
If vector search unavailable, matching uses domain + category match only
Accepted cross-workspace entries are copied into the target workspace's MEMORY.md with source attribution
Dismissed entries are recorded so they don't resurface
GET /api/memory/cross-workspace/:workspaceId returns suggested entries from other workspaces
POST /api/memory/cross-workspace/:workspaceId/accept/:entryId copies the entry
POST /api/memory/cross-workspace/:workspaceId/dismiss/:entryId suppresses it
